newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Negara Indonesia up on MSCI talk.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara Indonesia up on MSCI talk.

text.p: Shares of state-controlled Bank Negara Indonesia rose on Thursday on continued talk that the firm would be included in the Morgan Stanley Composite Index, brokers said.
"The rise was mostly due to market rumours that starting February 15, Morgan Stanley will include Bank Negara Indonesia in its index," a broker with a Singapore brokerage firm said.
"There is also another rumour saying its bad debts have been written-off, so its financial result will be better," he added.
At mid-afternoon, Bank Negara Indonesia was up 125 rupiah to 1,425 rupiah before easing back to 1,400 rupiah. It topped the active list with 66.3 million shares traded.
The bank was also active on the cross-board, trading at 1,400 rupiah on a volume of 8.1 million shares.
Brokers said there was also market talk that the bank's 1996 net income would be up 15 percent from 1995, when it reported net profit of 274 billion rupiah.
An investor relations official with Bank Negara declined to comment on the MSCI rumours. He said the bank would announce its 1996 results in the second week of February.
Mirza Adityaswara, an analyst of BZW Niaga Securities, attributed the rise more to expectations of better-than-expected 1996 earnings rather than the MSCI index.

"I expect the bank will book 1996 earnings in a range of 330 billion to 335 billion rupiah, slightly higher than company's expectation of 326 or 327 billion rupiah which it predicted at a meeting with analysts before the initial public offering last year," he said.
Bank Negara Indonesia was listed on the Jakarta exchange last November 25.
